notes: Handheld/belt-worn beltpack (99 x 135 x 43mm, 0.35kg / IP53) — not rack-mountable, so rackUnits omitted. Sourced from Clear-Com's own official HXII-BP Beltpack datasheet (Rev. Sept/2022), which lists exactly 4 physical connectors on the bottom panel: 3-pin XLR-F Powerline, RJ45 etherCON (LAN/PoE), Micro-AB USB (flasher), and the 4-pin XLR-M headset jack (X4 variant). There is no dedicated power-only inlet — power arrives either via PoE on the Ethernet port or via the XLR Powerline connection, so both are marked bidirectional rather than a separate "power in" port. All connectors here are analog/legacy or unspecified-speed digital, so no bandwidth "grade" was set on any port (per instructions, omitted whenever the spec doesn't state a version/speed). Retailer listings (Markertek, Full Compass, Sweetwater, BSW) corroborate the same connector set. Device is a 2-channel HelixNet digital partyline intercom beltpack, not a match for any of the provided "type" enum values, so type is set to "Other" (category "audio" fits well).

ports.name: XLR Powerline
ports.note: 3-pin XLR-F. Legacy analog partyline connection to an HMS-4X main station: carries 2-way intercom audio plus DC power (input voltage ±29.5V DC, 0.13A max). Not available when hosted by Arcadia.

ports.name: Ethernet Connector
ports.note: RJ45 etherCON. Network audio/control link to Arcadia or HMS-4X (via optional HLI-ET2 module) and PoE power input (IEEE 802.3af-2003 Class 1, 3.84W DC max draw). Port's own link speed not stated in datasheet (only recommended switch ports listed as 100/1000 Base-T), so no eth-* grade set.

ports.name: USB
ports.note: Micro AB connector, documented specifically as the "USB call signal flasher connection to a third-party USB light" — a call-indicator output, not a general data/host port. No data-rate stated.

ports.name: Headset
ports.note: 4-pin XLR-M headset jack (X4 variant only — the X5 variant uses a 5-pin XLR-F for binaural). Carries analog headset mic input and headphone output, NOT DC power — "xlr4-dc" was chosen only because it is the closest 4-pin XLR id in the allowed connector list; there is no generic 4-pin audio XLR option.
